quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold up your body.
Sit at an angle so your arms can support your weight.
Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit upright so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle. Your arms should not be used to hold up your body.

questions.question: How is the accelerator controlled?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip. You control it with your right hand.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Look over their shoulder when taking a turn or curve.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over their shoulder when taking a turn or curve.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to look over your shoulder in the direction you are turning. This helps both of you lean the motorcycle correctly for the turn.

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: May be shared by the driver and passenger
Are required for the driver and passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for good balance. Your motorcycle must have footrests for both you and your passenger. This keeps your passenger from falling off.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a traffic regulation sign. It is white with red and black markings. This sign means you cannot turn right in this area.

questions.question: To reduce the chances of a collision, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Stare straight in front of their motorcycle.
Be unwilling to move to avoid a potential hazard.
Scan their path of travel, looking at least 10 to 15 seconds ahead of their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Scan their path of travel, looking at least 10 to 15 seconds ahead of their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Look ahead 10 to 15 seconds down the road. Scanning ahead gives you time to react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a method used to maintain control of a motorcycle in a turn?
questions.explanation: To turn safely, slow down before you turn. Look through the turn in the direction you want to go. Lean into the turn. Then gently roll on the throttle as you go through the turn.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a potentially slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet pavement, snow, ice, mud, gravel roads, lane markings, and metal utility covers.

questions.question: To improve your chances of being seen, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight only at night or when conditions reduce visibility.
Add an orange tint to your headlight.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. This is the best way to make sure other drivers see your motorcycle.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:
questions.explanation: Always use both the front and rear brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which lane position makes a motorcyclist most visible to other drivers?
questions.explanation: The center lane position is best when following a car. It puts you in the driver's rearview mirror so they can see you. Always be ready to change positions if traffic or road conditions require it.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle provides the most stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of your motorcycle's stopping power. Use both the front and rear brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: When can a motorcycle pass on the right?

options.text: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
By riding on the shoulder of the road.
By riding on the grass, if it is level.

questions.correctAnswerText: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
questions.explanation: You can pass on the right only if there is at least eight feet of clear pavement to the right of the vehicle you are passing. Never leave the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do with your hands when carrying a package on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use one hand to steer and the other to hold the package.
Keep both hands on the handlebars.
Rest the package in front and hold it occasionally with your hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep both hands on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: You cannot carry anything that stops you from keeping both hands on the handlebars at all times.

questions.question: How should riders ride when traveling in a group?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. It keeps riders close together while giving each rider enough space. Use a single-file formation when turning, going through curves, entering a highway, or exiting a highway.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over bridge gratings, what should you do?

options.text: Downshift to a lower gear right away.
Weave side to side until you cross the bridge.

questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves on bridge gratings, relax and go straight across at a steady speed. Weaving side to side is more dangerous.

questions.question: Alcohol reaches the brain ________ being consumed.
questions.explanation: Alcohol reaches your brain within minutes and starts affecting your ability to ride. Riding under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to tell the other vehicle to go.
You should go through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: How should motorcyclists ride in a group on a straight road?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps the group close while giving each rider enough space. Use a single-file formation when turning, riding curves, or entering or leaving a road.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT strongly affect your blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.explanation: The main factors that affect BAC are the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Age does not play a major role.

questions.question: When should you use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch?

options.text: The throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
You start to lose control in a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: The throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
questions.explanation: If the throttle gets stuck, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch right away. This stops power to the rear wheel so you can safely leave the road and stop.

questions.question: When should riders use their headlights?
questions.explanation: Use your headlight all the time. Other drivers will see your headlight before they see your motorcycle. South Carolina law requires motorcycles to have their headlights on whenever the bike is being used.

questions.question: When riding ________, you face the greatest risk of conflict with other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. When you approach an intersection, ride in a position that makes you easy to see.

questions.question: What is the best way to help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Maintain eye contact with other road users.

questions.explanation: Using your headlight is the best way to help others see your motorcycle. Check that your headlight works before you start riding.

questions.question: What should you do when making a U-turn?

options.text: The front and rear brakes need to be used at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
Use the front brake to increase stability of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it can make the bike tip over. Instead, use the rear brake to control your speed.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Avoid making sudden moves, as doing so could cause a skid.
Travel on the shoulder to be out of the way of traffic.
Use only the rear brake because the front brake is ineffective on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making sudden moves, as doing so could cause a skid.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, any sudden change in speed or direction can cause a skid. Be smooth when you speed up, shift gears, turn, or brake.

questions.question: What is the correct way to shift gears in a curve?

options.text: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
Is better than shifting before the curve.
Is the best way to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
questions.explanation: It is best to change gears before starting a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden change in power can cause a skid.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do in high-risk areas?

options.text: Cover the clutch and both brake levers to reduce their reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and both brake levers to reduce their reaction time.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping areas, schools, and construction zones, cover the clutch and both brake levers. This lets you react faster in an emergency.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance when riding at night?
questions.explanation: At night, it is hard to judge distances. Keep at least three seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
Drivers may proceed through the intersection with caution.
Drivers must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must stop and wait for a signal that lets you turn in your direction.
